rules.description: Processing user-controlled object hierarchies inefficiently can lead to denial of service.

rules.cwe_name: Function Call With Incorrect Number of Arguments
rules.description: A function is invoked with extra trailing arguments that are ignored.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
rules.description: Instantiating a template using a user-controlled object is vulnerable to local file read and potential remote code execution.
Legacy category for incorrect handling or transformation of structured data.
If an object literal has two properties with the same name, the second property overwrites the first one, which makes the code hard to understand and error-prone.

rules.cwe_name: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion')
rules.description: Sanitizing an HTTP request parameter may be ineffective if the user controls its type.
Comparing the result of a typeof test against a string other than 'undefined', 'boolean', 'number', 'string', 'object', 'function' or 'symbol' is useless, since this comparison can never succeed.
Legacy category for cryptographic design or implementation weaknesses.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
rules.description: Functions recursively assigning properties on objects may be the cause of accidental modification of a built-in prototype object.
The 'eval' function and the 'Function' constructor execute strings as code. This is dangerous and impedes program analysis and understanding. Consequently, these two functions should not be used.

rules.cwe_name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')
rules.description: Attacker-controlled object keys modify Object prototype attributes.
Processing user-controlled object hierarchies inefficiently can lead to denial of service.
Assigning to a property of a primitive value has no effect and may trigger a runtime error.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
rules.description: Modifying an object obtained via a user-controlled property name may lead to accidental mutation of the built-in Object prototype, and possibly escalate to remote code execution or cross-site scripting.
Listing the same property twice in one object literal is redundant and may indicate a copy-paste mistake.

rules.cwe_name: Function Call With Incorrect Number of Arguments
rules.description: A function is invoked with extra trailing arguments that are ignored.
Using cookies without CSRF protection may allow malicious websites to submit requests on behalf of the user.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command ('Argument Injection')
rules.description: Forwarding command-line arguments to a child process executed within a shell may indirectly introduce command-line injection vulnerabilities.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
rules.description: Replacing a substring with itself has no effect and may indicate a mistake.
Trying to access a property of "null" or "undefined" will result in a runtime exception.
